usage: fleet-switchboard daemon [-h] {status,start,stop,restart} ...

One command for the daemon. `status` says whether it runs, how it was started,
its pid, since when and whether it is healthy. `stop` ends it (SIGTERM, only
to a pid the daemon record and run.lock agree on whose command is this
program's `run`; `launchctl bootout` under a loaded launchd job). `start`
begins it (launchd when its job exists, else the `ensure` path) and waits up
to 120 seconds for it to be healthy. `restart` is stop then start. No state
file is touched.

positional arguments:
  {status,start,stop,restart}
    status              running or not, how it was started, pid, since when,
                        healthy or not (exit 1 when not running or unhealthy)
    start               start the daemon and wait until it is healthy
    stop                stop the daemon and wait for run.lock to clear
    restart             stop then start; prints what it did and the seconds
                        taken

options:

usage: fleet-switchboard decisions [-h] [--repo OWNER/REPO]
                                   [--tier {cos,human,orchestrator,all}]
                                   [--json] [--fresh] [--watch]
                                   [--from SENDER]
                                   {list,escalate,batch,supersede,resolve,answer} ...

Decisions have tiers. An orchestrator never goes straight to you: it raises a
decision to the Chief of Staff (`report question` and the awaiting-cos label),
which resolves it with your standing orders or escalates it (the awaiting-user
label). `decisions [list]` prints the open ones: the issues with either label,
the permission requests and questions of every fleet agent, and the questions
and blocks workers reported that nobody has answered. The view depends on who
asks (you are identified by your pane): the Chief of Staff sees every repo and
tier; an orchestrator its own repo, every tier; anyone else only the human
tier. --repo and --tier override. It says which view it printed. By default it
reads decisions.json, which the daemon rewrites when the list changes; a file
older than 180 s is said to be stale, never shown as current. `escalate`,
`resolve` and `answer` are for the Chief of Staff (or you, in a plain shell).

positional arguments:
  {list,escalate,batch,supersede,resolve,answer}
    list                The open decisions in your view (the default)
    escalate            Move a decision to the owner (the awaiting-user label,
                        or at once for a permission request or question). Not
                        judged
    batch               Raise related findings as ONE decision: one issue in
                        your own repo, labelled for the Chief of Staff, one
                        row per finding
    supersede           Mark several open decisions superseded by one issue.
                        An issue decision: a comment and both labels off; a
                        report: your `send` to its worker. Judged like
                        `resolve`
    resolve             Take both awaiting labels off a decision's issue: it
                        is settled. Judged against the Chief of Staff's
                        standing orders
    answer              Answer an agent's pending permission request
                        (allow|deny) or question (the answer's text) through
                        v2, or a batch (--as-recommended, --row). Judged
                        against the Chief of Staff's standing orders

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo OWNER/REPO     Only this repo's decisions
  --tier {cos,human,orchestrator,all}
                        Only this tier: cos, human or orchestrator; all for
                        every tier
  --json                Emit the list as JSON (with `stale` and `view`)
  --fresh               Derive the list now instead of reading the file
  --watch               Redraw when the list changes, until Ctrl-C (a fallback
                        for a terminal without the TUI plugin)
  --from SENDER         Lab only: the caller's fleet name

usage: fleet-switchboard disk [-h] [--docker DOCKER]
                              {report,prune,reap-docker,janitor,janitor-ack,reap-orphans,reclaim-worktrees,register-worktree} ...

positional arguments:
  {report,prune,reap-docker,janitor,janitor-ack,reap-orphans,reclaim-worktrees,register-worktree}
    report              what holds the disk: free space, docker usage,
                        worktrees per agent, cache sizes, orphan candidates
                        (read only; also a bare `disk`)
    prune               docker builder prune, docker image prune -a (older
                        than a week) and, on docker 23.0 or newer, docker
                        volume prune -f (anonymous volumes only), and nothing
                        else
    reap-docker         remove EXPIRED docker containers, networks and volumes
                        that carry fleet.owner and fleet.expires labels
    janitor             remove old, unnamed entries of the opencode temp
                        directory (a dry run unless --apply)
    janitor-ack         record the yes to the temp janitor's would-remove
                        preview (the Chief of Staff's or the operator's)
    reap-orphans        Signal (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) orphaned test helpers
                        past the grace: parent launchd, an exact allow-list; a
                        dry run unless --apply
    reclaim-worktrees   Remove the registered worktrees of retired agents when
                        clean and pushed; else keep and say why (a dry run
                        unless --apply)
    register-worktree   Record a linked worktree for an agent (launch records
                        its own)

options:

usage: fleet-switchboard disk prune [-h] [--dry-run] [--docker DOCKER]

Runs exactly `docker builder prune -f --filter until=168h` and `docker image
prune -a -f --filter until=168h` and prints what was reclaimed, then (only
when the docker server is 23.0 or newer, where it removes ANONYMOUS volumes no
container references and nothing named) `docker volume prune -f`, never `-a`.
Never a running container, never `system prune`. Refuses without docker. NOTE:
`until=168h` is the image's age, not its last use: a locally built image with
no registry copy is removed too if no container uses it.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --dry-run        Print the commands and the candidate anonymous volumes and
                   run none of them
  --docker DOCKER  The docker executable (default: docker on PATH)

usage: fleet-switchboard disk reap-docker [-h] [--apply] [--docker DOCKER]

Lists (the default) or, with --apply, removes docker containers (`rm -f`),
networks and volumes that carry BOTH labels `fleet.owner=<agent>` and
`fleet.expires=<epoch seconds>` and whose expiry has passed. Never an
unlabelled object, a live one, or a volume a running container mounts; no
`system prune`, no sudo. The daemon applies this daily unless the config key
`docker_reaper` is false. Each removal is one `docker.reaped` audit line.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --apply          Remove them (the default only lists)
  --docker DOCKER  The docker executable (default: docker on PATH)

usage: fleet-switchboard disk janitor [-h] [--apply]
                                      [--i-reviewed FINGERPRINT] [--weekly]

Lists (the default) or, with --apply, removes the top-level entries of the
temp directory whose newest file is older than temp_janitor.days (default 7)
and that no state file of the fleet names, no keep glob matches and no .fleet-
keep marker protects. Never follows a link, never touches another user's
entry. Each removal is one temp.removed audit line.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --apply               Remove them (the default only lists)
  --i-reviewed FINGERPRINT
                        With --apply: the preview fingerprint the dry run
                        printed. Refused when it no longer matches the rule
                        and the listed names
  --weekly              The weekly job: scan under the longer budget
                        temp_janitor.weekly_scan_seconds (default 600 s)
                        instead of scan_seconds (60 s)

usage: fleet-switchboard disk janitor-ack [-h] preview

The daemon sends the Chief of Staff one would-remove preview after any change
of the janitor's selection rule and applies nothing until the yes to that
exact preview is recorded here. A changed rule makes a new preview and needs a
new yes.

positional arguments:
  preview     the preview's fingerprint, as the message gives it
